To further amplify the harassment, perpetrators often use bots or scripts to automate certain tasks.  This might involve automatically retweeting harassing content, liking negative comments, or mass-following the victim to create a sense of being watched and overwhelmed.  They also frequently leverage the platform’s reporting mechanisms – falsely reporting the victim’s accounts for policy violations in an attempt to get them suspended or banned.  This is known as “report bombing.” Creating echo chambers, where fake accounts interact exclusively with each other to reinforce the harassment, is also used to create a distorted perception of public opinion.

Finally, the goal isn’t always immediate, overt damage. Sometimes it’s sustained psychological distress, forcing the victim to disengage from online spaces or become overwhelmed by the constant negativity.  The anonymity and sheer volume of the attack can be deeply demoralizing, leading to anxiety, depression, and even suicidal thoughts. The perpetrators may also attempt to "gaslight" the victim, denying the harassment or distorting events to make the victim question their own sanity.
